samples.summary: No test that a CUT paste still refuses when it clips a merged block that is NOT part of the cut
samples.evidence: The delta weakens the split-guard for cuts (`planPasteMerges` filters `getMergesIntersecting(destRange)` by a `travelling` set when `isCut`). The only test covering the weakened path is the new one at merge.test.ts:528, which asserts the *non*-refusal direction (its own block). The one refusal test, 'should refuse a paste that would split a destination block' (merge.test.ts:476-502), uses `sheet.copy()`, so it exercises `isCut === false` only. I grepped every `sheet.cut()` call in packages/sheets/test (merge.test.ts:395, 540 and clipboard.test.ts) and none combines a cut with a destination that clips a foreign merged block. Consequence: if the exclusion were over-broad (e.g. skipping the check entirely for cuts, or a wrong anchor comparison), a cut paste would split a destination merge and corrupt the merge map with a green suite.

samples.summary: New cut test does not assert the clipped source cells / stale data left behind by the moved block
samples.evidence: The new test asserts only `refusals`, `merges.size === 1`, `merges.get('D2')` and the value at r2,c4. It does not check that the old covered cell C2 (which is inside both the cut source range and the destination region) holds no stale value, nor that B2 is cleared. Since the whole point of the exclusion is that the cut deletes its block at the source while the destination overlaps it, residual content/alias state in the overlap region is exactly the failure mode this test is meant to guard and it is unasserted.
searchedFor: read paste()/cut source-deletion logic in sheet.ts:2354-2367

verdict.reason: The cut-specific branch of the paste split-guard has no refusal test anywhere in the repo. planPasteMerges (sheet.ts:2428-2440) excludes only the cut's own merge anchors via `travelling` and must still refuse when the destination clips a foreign block (sheet.ts:2260-2263). The single test asserting 'merge-paste-partial' (merge.test.ts:476-502, assertion at :496) uses sheet.copy() at :490, so isCut === false. The two cut tests (merge.test.ts:386-405 with no foreign block; :528-552 asserting refusals === [] for its own block) both pass even if the check were skipped entirely for cuts, and no other cut test drops a foreign destination block (the 'fully covers' test at :407-427 also uses copy). I searched wider than the reviewer: every `refus*` assertion in packages/sheets tests, every file referencing mergeSelection/getMerges repo-wide, clipboard.test.ts and packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-cut-paste.test.ts (neither mentions 'merge'), and all *.test.* files for related wording. No counterexample found. Impact if the exclusion is over-broad: a cut paste silently splits a destination merge and corrupts the merge map with a green suite — user-visible/data-affecting, so blocking under the missing-test branch of the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: No test for cut-paste of a merged block into a destination that overlaps the source
finding.evidence: The new code has an explicit branch for exactly this case — `applyPasteMerges` builds a `dropped` Map with the comment "A cut whose destination overlaps its source can name the same block twice; deleting it once is enough" (sheet.ts ~2447) — and `planPasteMerges` will also see the source block partially inside the shifted destination range, which would make it return `undefined` and refuse the whole cut. No test in the new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block exercises an overlapping cut with a merge: 'should drop a cut merged block at the source' cuts A1:B1 and pastes at A3 (disjoint). The existing clipboard suite has an 'cut overlapping destination (A1:B1 from A1:B1, paste at B1)' case (packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts:596) proving this is a real user path, but it has no merges. So whether an overlapping merged cut moves, refuses, or leaves a dangling/duplicated merge entry is completely unverified.

verdict.reason: A direct counterexample exists in the very file and describe block the finding says lacks it. packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:528 ('should not refuse a cut whose destination clips its own block') merges B2:C2 (lines 534-536), cuts A1:C3 (lines 538-540), and pastes at C1 (lines 544-545) — destination C1:E3 overlaps the source A1:C3 in column C, with the merged block B2:C2 only partially inside the shifted destination. That is exactly the path guarded by the `travelling` exclusion in planPasteMerges (sheet.ts:2432-2440, which would otherwise return undefined and refuse the cut) and by applyPasteMerges' dedup drop (sheet.ts:2468-2480). The assertions are meaningful and discriminate all three outcomes the finding calls unverified: refusals empty (line 547) fails if the cut is refused; merges.size === 1 (line 548) fails on a duplicated or dangling merge entry; merges.get('D2') === {rs:1,cs:2} and toDisplayString({r:2,c:4}) === '10' (lines 550-551) fail if the block does not move correctly with its content. The finding's claim that the only cut case in the new block is the disjoint A1:B1 -> A3 case (line 386) is factually wrong for this file. The only untested sub-aspect is the `dropped` Map de-duplicating a literally repeated anchor, which is defensive and subsumed by the merges.size assertion — not a blocking test-adequacy gap.
